inputs.text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement is a warning that years of unresolved commitments can bring universities to a standstill. But an indefinite nationwide strike would punish students and families as well as put pressure on government. The authorities should negotiate in good faith and honor legitimate obligations; unions, in turn, should recognize that shutting down education is not a cost-free way to make their case. Institutions need dependable staff and responsible leadership—not a cycle of promises and disruption.
